# Synthetic comparator-format fixtures

Every number, identifier, label and timestamp here is fabricated. There are no prompts, responses, filesystem paths, host names, credentials, real message or request identifiers, ledger rows, or vendor captures. Labels such as `fab-msg-n01a` and `fab-ledger-v03` are invented. The `-06:00` offset is used so that results do not depend on a time zone database; the one case that does use an IANA zone (`legacy-comparator-output`) says so in its `case.json`.

These fixtures pin the formats specified in `docs/reviews/2026-10-18-comparator-formats/FORMATS.md`. They are inputs and outputs of the reference code in `scripts/comparator-formats.py`, exercised by `scripts/test-comparator-formats.py`. They are not telemetry, a benchmark population, a vendor baseline, or release evidence, and nothing here closes a count gate.

## Layout

Each directory under `cases/` is one cohort pair. Side A is the subject (product ledger rows or native lines under test); side B is the reference (a vendor-style daily report or an independent native reading). `delta = A - B` and percentages are relative to B.

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `case.json` | What the case shows and does not show, normalization parameters, and the **hand-written expectations** (derived by hand from the rules, not from the code) |
| `a.input.json`, `b.input.json` | Raw side inputs in their source shape (ledger rows, ccusage-style daily report, native assistant lines, local-engine counters) |
| `a.cohort.json`, `b.cohort.json` | Golden canonical cohorts produced by the reference normalizer |
| `result.json` | Golden comparison result |

The golden files are generated by `python3 -I -B scripts/comparator-formats.py build-case --case-dir <dir> --write`. Because a generated file can only prove that output did not change, the tests also check every case against the hand-written `expect` block in `case.json`. A golden file and its expectations disagreeing is a test failure in either direction.

## Cases

| Case | What it pins |
| --- | --- |
| `v01-vendor-exact-match` | Vendor flat cache creation against a product three-way split; the split is compared only where both sides have it; vendor cost and model fields are never read |
| `v02-vendor-missing-vs-zero` | Absent vendor key (missing) against explicit 0 (measured zero); a vendor day that does not exist is only-in-subject, not a zero day |
| `v03-vendor-totals-equal-components-differ` | Equal totals, every component different; flagged, outcome `differs`; per-unit tolerance reporting |
| `v04-vendor-partial-day` | A partially readable day whose readable rows equal the reference total is still partial: no total, no match |
| `n01-native-iterations-shared-request` | Several usage iterations sharing one request id are summed per component; top-level usage mirroring the final iteration is not added again |
| `n02-native-snapshots-incomparable` | Per-field maxima (subtotal 118) held as conflict with no total; a stored conflict row keeps its numbers as inspection values only |
| `n03-native-requestless-messages` | Requestless identical snapshots across local midnight are one record at the later time; uuid-fallback identity; replay collapses |
| `n03d-requestless-vendor-double-count` | Day-level shape of a fabricated vendor day that counts a requestless message on two dates |
| `n04-native-resumed-session` | A resumed session replays earlier messages and grows one; identity is the message, not the session; no double counting |
| `n05-native-cache-ttl-split` | Flat-only (unassigned), full 5m/1h split, partial split, absent flat total, split above flat total, and a policy-assigned 1h that is never compared as reported TTL |
| `n06-native-missing-vs-zero-vs-invalid` | Absent, zero, null, negative and fractional counters are five different states; reasoning clamp; five line kinds that become no record; an unreadable line makes the cohort partial |
| `n07-local-engine-counters` | The six native-counter shapes of `test/fixtures/claude-cloud-2026-10-17/structure-only.json`; cache-write categories not applicable; missing cache counter is not promoted to assume-zero |
| `legacy-comparator-output` | Real output of `scripts/compare-claude-ccusage.py` on an owned synthetic database, mapped into canonical day cohorts; shows which facts that output cannot express |

## Refusals

`refusals/` holds eight inputs that must be refused with a fixed code, and one cohort document with a duplicated identity that the validator must report, listed in `refusals/manifest.json`: duplicate ledger id, duplicate vendor day, duplicate local-engine event id, a duplicate record in a cohort, an unsupported ledger schema or projection policy, an unknown stored count quality, an impossible vendor date, and a native line that is not an object. A duplicate identity is refused, never merged and never resolved by keeping one row. (Replayed native *lines* of one message are different: they are snapshots and collapse; see `n03` and `n04`.)

## What these fixtures do not show

They do not show how any real vendor version, the real collector, or any real ledger behaves; the values were chosen to exercise the rules. `n03d` in particular is an invented illustration of the shape described in a dated continuation document, not a measurement of any vendor version. Hand arithmetic in `n01`, `n02`, `n03` and `n04` reuses the numbers of the existing native reference tests (`scripts/check-native-*-reference.test.mjs`) so the expected counts stay checkable by eye; agreement with those tests' arithmetic is not agreement with the product collector.

The fixtures cannot close the original 1% count gate, exact native-50, per-thread or vendor baselines, or any acceptance item. They create no benchmark population and run no vendor capture.
